RelationTypes.title: Relation types
RelationTypes.intro: Define recurring labels with their inverse and, if you like, the categories that may be linked. Relations whose label matches a type follow its constraints; others stay free-form.
RelationTypes.empty: No relation types yet. Free-form relations work regardless.
RelationTypes.label: Label
RelationTypes.constraintHint: With a category chosen, only snippets of that category can be linked with this label. Existing relations do not change. Renaming or deleting a type does not change existing relations, which keep their label (now free-form).
RelationTypes.readOnly: Only owners and editors can edit types.

Calendars.title: Calendars
Calendars.intro: Define your world’s calendars: months, weekdays, eras and a periodic long year. Then use them in the “calendar date” fields of your categories: dates compare and sort without depending on the real calendar.
Calendars.empty: No calendars yet. Create one to use dates from your world.
Calendars.summary: {months, plural, one {# month} other {# months}}, {days} days a year, {weekdays, plural, one {# weekday} other {# weekdays}}, {eras, plural, one {# era} other {# eras}}.
Calendars.name: Name
Calendars.monthsHint: One per line: name, days (for example “Dawn, 30”). The order is the order of the year.
Calendars.epochWeekday: Weekday of the first day of year 0 (number, from 1)
Calendars.erasHint: One per line: name, start year (for example “Second Age, 100”). Years count from 1 inside each era; year 0 and negative years exist.
Calendars.leapHint: Every so many years one month gets extra days, like 29 February.
Calendars.readOnly: Only owners and editors can change calendars.

notices.deleted: Calendar deleted. Dates already written in snippets stay.

errors.invalid_leap: Invalid long year: it needs every how many years (at least 2), an existing month and the extra days.

errors.duplicate: A calendar with this name already exists.

Timeline.intro: Snippets with a date in one of the world’s calendars, laid out in time: point or interval events, in lanes by category or tag. Each event links to its snippet.

Timeline.lanesTruncated: The first 30 lanes are shown: narrow down with a filter.

Maps.intro: Upload images of your maps (a region, a city, a dungeon), mark places with pins and draw routes. If a map depicts a place, the pin on that place opens its map.

Tree.title: Tree and hierarchy
Tree.intro: Pick a relation label and see the same world as a tree: a family tree with “parent of”, a chain of command with “commands”, a sequence of chapters with “follows”…

Tree.labelHint: A relation “A parent of B” puts A above B. The inverse label works too: if “B child of A” has “parent of” as its inverse, the tree is the same.
Tree.root: Start from (title of a snippet, optional)
Tree.pickHint: Pick a label to build the tree.

Campaigns.title: Campaigns
Campaigns.intro: A campaign brings a DM and their players together. It can be linked to a world or stand alone; you join with an invite.

Campaigns.linkedOther: Linked to a world you cannot see
Campaigns.name: Campaign name
Campaigns.worldHint: You can only link a world you belong to. The DM can change it later.
Campaigns.caption: Campaign members and their roles
Campaigns.invitesIntro: An invite is a link: whoever opens it, once signed in, joins with the chosen role. With an email the invite only works for that account. You share the link yourself: the app does not send emails.

Visibility.title: Visibility and reveals
Visibility.intro: Decide who sees this snippet and each of its fields. “DM only” is for those who write in the world (the DM) only; “Chosen players” only for the members you pick; “All members” and “Public” for everyone else. Every change is logged.
Visibility.usersHint: They apply to every item in this form set to “Chosen players”. You pick among members who do not write in the world.
Visibility.noPlayers: No players: add readers or commenters from the world members panel to be able to share with them.
Visibility.fieldsHint: A field is never more visible than its snippet. “Same as snippet” brings it back to the snippet level.
Visibility.note: Note (optional), for example what was revealed and why. Recipients of a reveal can read it too.
